MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 25, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley at 5:02 p.m., on April 25, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 20, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:02pm)
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell (arrived at 5:03pm)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with legal Counsel: Threat to Public Services or Facilities; Consultation
  with City Attorney and Director of Information Technology David Meyer

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:07p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  April 25, 2023
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council reviewed some security issues but
nothing disclosable to report.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation to the City Council from Supervisor Don Wagner

  Received presentation from Supervisor Don Wagner.

P2. Proclamation April 29th as World Wish Day in the City of Mission Viejo

  Mayor Goodell presented the proclamation to Karen Lindgren a volunteer at Make-A-Wish
  Orange County and the Inland Empire.

P3. Presentation of the Core Area Vision Plan and Launch of the Community
  Communication Campaign

  Received presentation from Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following spoke on the outstanding presentation and in favor of the Core Area Vision Plan
and Launch of the Community Campaign; Andy Steen, M.V., Sara Vandenbrock, Rancho Mission
Viejo, Nancy Silver, M.V., Greg Silver, M.V., Tom Ross, M.V., Eric Chastain, M.V., and Larry
Ryan, M.V.

Eric Cernich, Newport Beach: Complemented Mr. Rattay on a phenomenal presentation. Stated
he owns Trader Joe’s and Party City, and is also a real estate developer. He mentioned that in
2015 he brought a plan to redevelop the center to the City Council, and they turned down his
concept. Added that he is happy to hear the City is open to public/private partnership, and would
be interested in working together with the City on this project. Lastly, he requested a copy of the
City’s CC&R’s and of the easement for the City’s use of the trial on his property.

Wade Weiman, M.V.: Stated he’s with “The Patio” in the center, and listed the four retail stores.
He commended Keith on his presentation. He shared concerns of the CC&R’s not being followed
by the City and parking issues during the Farmers Market. He stated that a committee was formed
with some parcel owners and city staff. He concluded by stating he was not aware of this
presentation and asked for better communication going forward.

Mindy Geller, M.V.: Complemented Keith on a great presentation and concept, however she
voiced concerns related to parking. She represents “The Patio” and mentioned there is no
City Council Minutes  2  April 25, 2023
 discussion on parking, which is a major problem. She stated better communication is needed with
the owners. She requested to see the traffic study which she feels it is not accurate if performed
during COVID. Lastly, she mentioned cost needs to be shared with residents as this is not a cheap
investment.

City Attorney Bill Curley addressed some of the comments pertaining to the CC&R’s, and stated
that the City studied them carefully. He clarified that Ms. Kronick’s attorney approached the City
and together they have been working on a pending Management Agreement, and new and revised
CC&R’s. Finally, he added that an upcoming meeting has been postponed by the property owners
until the Agreement is finalized.

Tom Moore, M.V.: Complemented Keith on a great presentation. Spoke in favor of the Core Area
Vision Plan.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Stated he represents Stopthemonster.org. Complemented Keith on a great
presentation. Gave an update on his second meeting with AvalonBay, and stated he is losing trust
with AvalonBay and Value Rock as he is getting mixed messages. He met with Development
Consultant Timothy Grizzell at Garden Plaza, who mentioned they are only interested in building
apartments, plus other buildings for businesses and not offering any housing for low income
families.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Was happy to hear the presentation by Supervisor Don Wagner. However,
he voiced his concern over safety at Mission Viejo schools, meetings, concerts, etc. He referred
to a personal experience, over 25 years ago, of a school that had strict security measures in place
and concluded by saying, the time has come for our city to harden its perimeter.

Michelle O’Brien, M.V.: Shared that in March the Elks Lodge #2444, donated $24,200 to various
organizations, and announced their upcoming Inaugural Ball on April 29. She thanked the city for
hosting a great Earth/Arbor Day. And lastly, she thanked Council Member Bucknum for placing
item #20 on this evening’s agenda.

Christopher Hammer, M.V.: Addressed his concerns regarding Los Osos, Oso Creek and Core
Area Vision Plan. He voiced concerns on wildlife and requested an environmental impact report
and for the City to conduct a nature study. Lastly, he spoke in favor of licensing for E-Bikes.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9, 10, 11 and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  3  April 25, 2023
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the regular City Council Minutes for he Meeting of April 11, 2023, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated March 31, 2023 in the Amount of $172,062.03

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated April 7, 2023 in the Amount of $4,010,786.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated March 31, 2023 in the Amount of $10,497.99

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

  Approved purchase order to Optiv Security Inc. in amount not to exceed $32,696.56 for

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  April 25, 2023
 9.  Purchase (1) Electric Vehicle - Replacement City Carpool Vehicle

  Public Services Director Jerry Hill answered Council Member Vasquez’s questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize the City Manager to issue a Purchase Order for an Electric Vehicle in an amount
  not to exceed $37,000.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10. Annual Routine Monthly Landscape Maintenance - Contract Area 9

  Public Services Director Jerry Hill answered Council Member Vasquez’s questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)
  approve Eighth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Landscape West
  Management Services, Inc; (2) authorize a Change Order to the existing Purchase Order for
  Landscape West Management Services, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $14,964.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11. Annual Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract

  Public Services Director Jerry Hill answered Council Member Vasquez’s questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Vasquez, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)
  approve Second Amendment, County Agreement # MA-080-23010587, with the County of
  Orange for the period July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2025 in the amount of $2,255,254.00;
  and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July
  1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 in an amount not to exceed $1,127,627.00, pending adoption
  of the 2023-2025 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  April 25, 2023
 12. Purchase of One (1) Replacement Vehicle for Mission Viejo Police Services

  Emergency Preparedness Manager Paul Catsimanes answered Council Member Ruesch’s
  questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize the City Manager to Purchase a Replacement Vehicle for Mission Police Services
  in an Amount not to exceed $56,000.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

14. FY 2023-2025 Proposed CIP Budget

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

  By consensus the City Council received the report.

15. Professional Services Agreement for Planning Services to Develop Objective Design
  Standards for New Residential Development

  Planning and Economic Development Manager Jennifer Lowe presented the staff report.

  Carlos Pianelli, M.V: Stated the Council’s leadership protected the City last year, and
  mentioned the upcoming anniversary of May 10, and that the Council is protecting the City
  again this year. He added that July 2 marks the implementation of new housing laws, and
  asked if by authorizing a consultant, is the City protected or can someone come in and hinder
  the Core Area Vision Plan. Lastly, he asked if it is possible to place Olympic rings in the
  Core Area.

  Council Members asked various questions of staff and the City Attorney.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  authorize (1) authorize the City Manager to negotiate an agreement not to exceed $150,000
  for Development of Objective Design Standards for New Residential Development; and (2)
  adopt Resolution 23-14 Amending the FY 2022/2023 Advanced Planning Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  6  April 25, 2023
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

Item taken out of order

Council Member Bucknum

20. Opposition of AB 1078 (Corey Jackson 2023)-Pertaining to the Removal of Local
  Authority from School Boards

  Council Member Bucknum spoke on the letter of opposition, the removal of local decision
  making from local government entities to determine what the best policy is for their local
  school districts.

  Council Member Vasquez stated that she is currently a parent of children in Mission Viejo
  schools, and this opposition puts people squarely against teachers. She added she is all for
  local control, but feels like this is an attack on teachers and administrators who get paid very
  little for such a vital profession. Furthermore, Council Member Vasquez stated this is a
  School District issue and not a municipal one, and as such, it distracts from important work
  the city should be focusing on.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Thanked Council Member Bucknum for bringing this vital issue to the
  Councils attention. He spoke in opposition to AB 1078, how this is just another attempt for
  Sacramento to strip away from cities and School Boards the right to determine their own fate,
  how it must be stopped, and that he fully supports the Council sending the letter of opposition.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve
  sending a letter of opposition.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT:  None

16. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

17. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

18. Discussion on City Issued E-BIKE license Plates
City Council Minutes  7  April 25, 2023
   Chief of Police Chris McDonald presented the staff report.

  Linda Shepard, M.V.: Suggested working with bike stores and schools regarding E-Bike
  safety. She supports safety training for youth and their parents, and approves of having a
  bike license. She also spoke in support of opposing AB 1078. Lastly, she mentioned that as
  of January 1, 2023, SB 107 passed providing refuge for trans kids and their families.

  Council Members asked various questions of staff and Chief of Police Chris McDonald.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined the events she attended; SCAG Legislative Summit, Earth
Day/Arbor Day and gave kudos to all that attended as they ran out of plants, National Prescription
Day, she thanked OCSD and volunteers, Multicultural Medley Event. She gave a special shout out
to the Capo Mariachi Band and kudos to all who put the event on. Council Member Bucknum also
recognized and congratulated Kimberly Schmitt, for receiving the City Clerk of the Year Award
for the State of California.

Council Member Ruesch

Council Member Ruesch stated that Council Member Bucknum covered the incredible
Multicultural Medley Event and the that North Paseo events just keep getting better. He added
that he also attends the Chamber of Commerce Daybreakers Meetings on a regular basis. Council
Member Ruesch mentioned that last week the OCFA invited him to attend the AirEx 2023 event
at John Wayne Airport, a simulated aircraft accident with passengers. This drill took eight months
of preparation, and was incredibly organized engaging all resources in South County. Lastly, he
confirmed that after Lora Young’s (Director of Vector Control) update on mosquitos at the last
Council Meeting, that Mission Viejo has been selected as one of two test areas to see if sterile
insect control actually works.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez announced that she attended Senator Catherine Blakespear’s Leadership
Roundtable, as did Mayor Goodell and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley. She found it very productive, and
added that everyone is on the same page when it comes to local control on housing. She also
attended Earth Day/Arbor Day with her family, the Multicultural Medley Event and commented
on the awesome Mariachi Band, and lastly the National Prescription Day. To conclude, Council
Member Vasquez said that her eldest daughter came home from school today and mentioned that
City Council Minutes  8  April 25, 2023
 she and her fellow students would like to hear more about the water treatment plant at Council
Meetings.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley gave a huge congratulations to Kimberly Schmitt for being recognized as
City Clerk of the Year for the State of California. She added it was quite a year and Kim handled
everything with confidence, professionalism and a smile, and is much appreciated by the Council.
She attended the Spring Boutique put on by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee, the
Roundtable with Senator Catherine Blakespear, and discussed housing mandates and bills, and
sober living issues, asking for assistance in these areas. She also attended Earth Day/Arbor Day
and thanked Director Jerry Hill and his staff for putting on such a well thought out and successful
event. Unfortunately, she missed the Multicultural Medley Event as she took her granddaughter
and three friends to see Cinderella at Mission Viejo High School.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell stated that he received a letter from the Arbor Day Foundation congratulating
Mission Viejo as a 2022 Tree City USA and read an excerpt from the press release. He gave a
brief outline of his trip to Brisbane, Australia, in an effort to recruit Olympic Committees to look
at Mission Viejo as a training base for the 2028 Olympics and will give a more complete report at
the next Council Meeting. He reunited with a fellow Olympian he had competed against in the
1976 Olympics that he had not seen 47 years. Mayor Goodell also attended the Chamber of
Commerce Mixer at All Star Pizza with Congresswoman Kim in attendance, the Roundtable with
Senator Catherine Blakespear. He met with CHOC (Children's Hospital of Orange County) to talk
about their needs. Lastly, he closed the meeting in honor of Caltrans workers who have lost their
lives in serving our County, and announced that on April 29, Caltrans are celebrating those lives
lost.

ADJOURNMENT AT 10:15 PM TO TUESDAY, MAY 9, 2023, AT 5:00 P.M.

______________________________________
Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 9, 2023
